metadata.description: Concurrent multi-agent orchestration on Jujutsu (jj) workspaces for Claude Code

plugins.name: jj-concurrent
plugins.description: Orchestrator + worker model for running many Claude agents concurrently on jj workspaces: the jj-delegate mechanism, the jj-workspace-worker agent, a snapshot hook (closes jj's crash-before-snapshot gap) and a guard hook (blocks raw mutating git, interactive jj, and destructive ops on the jj/git stores). Workflow-agnostic; useful in any jj repo.

plugins.name: jj-concurrent-openspec
plugins.description: OpenSpec binding over jj-concurrent: /jj-openspec backgrounds an OpenSpec verb (apply / propose / new / ff) in its own jj workspace, mapping verb to shape (implementing vs authoring) and reconcile tail. Enable only in OpenSpec repos; requires the jj-concurrent plugin and the opsx skills.

plugins.name: jj-concurrent-linear
plugins.description: Linear binding over jj-concurrent: at the orchestrator's reconcile point, maps each worker's structured JSON report to its Linear sub-issue (in-progress → done on a clean finish, blocker/conflict comments otherwise), threading umbrella + sub-issue IDs from dispatch keyed by workspace path. Separate, separately-enabled binding; enable only in Linear-tracked repos. Requires the jj-concurrent plugin and a configured Linear MCP server. No issue creation, no PR cross-linking; the worker stays Linear-agnostic.

plugins.name: jj-lifecycle
plugins.description: Solo jj→GitHub lifecycle skills, decoupled from concurrency and OpenSpec: /jj-release cuts a GitHub release for the repo at a commit — relay-shaped prepare→go/no-go gate→publish, tag-only vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH versioning with an always-confirmed SemVer bump, notes generated from commits/PRs and editable in-conversation, a CI gate read off the target commit's check-runs/status, a 0.x→--prerelease-ON policy, an optional opaque artifacts hook, and server-side tag creation via gh release create --target; orchestrator-only, non-interactive, refuses to overwrite an existing release. Installable on its own — no concurrency or OpenSpec plugin required.
